contexts.text: To repair the brick kiln () = worship thence.
The smoke of the land as the smoke of a furnace () = the state of falsity, which is smoke, from the state of evil, which is a furnace, within the Church, which is the land.
From himself man is nothing but evil, which continually exhales as from a furnace.
The ash of a furnace () = of exciting the falsities of cupidities by presence with those who are infesting... The ashes of a furnace = the falsities of cupidities. AC 7519:5.

As the evils of cupidities are signified by fire, they are also signified by a furnace. A furnace is the containant, which often involves the same as the thing contained. That a furnace = these things. Illustrated.
Burning as a furnace () = the cupidities of evil.
The smoke of a furnace () = falsities from the evils of cupidities.
The smoke of a furnace () = ... falsities from the evils of cupidities.
The brick kiln () = the falsities which they invent, and which are injected by the evil.
The brick kiln () = the cupidity of falsity from evil.
Its smoke went up as the smoke of a furnace () = an obscurity like the obscurity from cupidities... A furnace = cupidity.
(The heat exhaling from the Hells when closed is) in some places like that from a heated oven.
That pit, which is like the opening of a furnace...
He opened the pit of the abyss, and there went up a smoke out of the pit as the smoke of a great furnace () = the falsities of the concupiscences of the natural man springing from their evil loves.
The fire of Hell = evil love; in like manner a great furnace, because this smokes from fire.
Love, when excited, appears... outside the Hells as... the smoke of a furnace.
The falsities of the concupiscences springing from evil loves are also described elsewhere in the Word by smoke from a lire and from a furnace. Illustrated.
He sank down, first into fire... then into fiery smoke as of a furnace; presently, under that furnace; for the place was represented as the place of a great furnace.
(The lighted furnace through which David made his enemies pass. ). Described.
She had borne a child and had thrown it into a furnace. SE 4504.
There opened the entrance as of a great furnace tending into the deep... After some torments she escaped...
The doctrine thence is called a brick kiln (), from the fact that infernal love is made stable by things falsified.
There went up a smoke out of the pit, as the smoke of a great furnace = dense falsities from the evils of earthly and corporeal loves... A great furnace = the evils of earthly and corporeal loves.
As that people was in earthly and corporeal loves, and thence in the falsities of evil, the Lord from mount Sinai appeared to them as... the smoke of a furnace.

It is important to show that a furnace = the evils of earthly and corporeal loves... That a furnace = these loves, is from the appearances in the Spiritual World; for the Hells in which those loves reign... appear like furnaces glowing with fire, and above them there appears smoke such as that which ascends from furnaces... Hence it is that in the Word furnaces = either the Hells, or a congregation of men, or a man himself, in whom such loves and cupidities reign; or, what is the same, where the evils from them are springing forth. These things are signified by furnaces, furnaces, furnaces, and ovens, in the following places. Illustrated.
To repair the brick kiln = to repair the doctrine compacted of falsified truths and figments.
By the great stones hidden in the brick kiln () are signified the truths of the Word falsified by figments which are from Own intelligence... The brick kiln = doctrine compacted of fictitious things.
As by Egypt is signified the natural man as to the Scientific there, and by a furnace of iron in like manner, therefore Egypt in the Word is called a furnace of iron. Illustrated.
The natural man as to the Scientific is signified by a furnace of iron; a furnace = the natural man; and iron, the Scientific...
The evils which are to be dispersed by that Church are signified by, Like a furnace among the wood, and like a torch in a sheaf ().
